content.value_statement: Service mesh routing can be difficult to configure safely across many services. This skill provides Istio templates and guidance for routing, canary releases, retries, load balancing, gateways, and resilience controls.
actual_capabilities: Explains Istio traffic resources including VirtualService, DestinationRule, Gateway, and ServiceEntry.
Provides YAML templates for routing, canary deployment, circuit breaking, retries, and timeouts.
Shows traffic mirroring and fault injection patterns for controlled testing.
Covers load balancing options including round robin and consistent hashing.
Includes ingress gateway examples for HTTPS hosts and path routing.
Lists istioctl commands for analyzing routes, endpoints, and proxy logs.
limitations: It does not inspect a live cluster or validate manifests automatically.
Examples use placeholder service names, namespaces, and hosts that must be adapted.
It does not replace an Istio version compatibility review.
Production changes still require rollout controls, observability, and approval.

use_cases.title: Plan Canary Releases
use_cases.description: Create weighted routing plans and subset policies before shifting traffic to a new service version.

use_cases.title: Standardize Mesh Routing
use_cases.description: Draft consistent VirtualService and DestinationRule patterns for platform teams that manage shared clusters.

use_cases.title: Improve Service Resilience
use_cases.description: Add timeouts, retries, connection pools, and outlier detection to reduce cascading failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft an Istio VirtualService and DestinationRule for service <name> with stable subset v1 and canary subset v2.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Canary Traffic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a canary rollout plan for <service>. Include traffic weights, subset labels, checks, and rollback conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Resilience Policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design DestinationRule and VirtualService settings for timeouts, retries, connection pools, and outlier detection for <service>.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Mesh Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review these Istio manifests for routing conflicts, gateway exposure, mirror targets, fault injection, and operational risks: <paste manifests>.

output_examples.input: Request: Build canary traffic management for payments at 95 percent stable and 5 percent canary.
output_examples.output: A rollout plan with weighted routing, subset requirements, health checks, telemetry checks, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Request: Add circuit breaker controls for the ratings service.
output: Recommended connection pool limits for TCP and HTTP traffic.
Retry and timeout guidance that avoids excessive retries.
Outlier detection thresholds and monitoring checks.

output_examples.input: Request: Review an ingress gateway design for an API host.
output_examples.output: A review covering host matching, TLS secret requirements, path routing, and validation commands.

best_practices: Start with small traffic percentages and increase only after telemetry is healthy.
Set explicit timeouts, retry limits, and outlier detection for user-facing services.
Validate generated manifests in a staging cluster before production use.
anti_patterns: Applying placeholder manifests without changing service names, labels, and namespaces.
Mirroring sensitive production traffic into test systems without data controls.
Using fault injection against production services without a defined experiment window.

faq.question: Does this skill apply manifests?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and guidance. The user or agent must choose and run deployment commands separately.

faq.question: Which Istio resources does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers VirtualService, DestinationRule, Gateway, ServiceEntry concepts, and common traffic policies.

faq.question: Can it help with canary deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes weighted routing examples and rollout guidance for stable and canary subsets.

faq.question: Does it require live cluster access?
faq.answer: No. Live validation needs external tools such as istioctl and kubectl in your environment.

faq.question: Is it safe for production?
faq.answer: It can support production planning, but generated policies need review, staging validation, and monitoring.

faq.question: Does it cover security policy?
faq.answer: It focuses on traffic management, not authorization, mTLS setup, or identity policy.
